    Functional Biomass (Functional Pool). Functional biomass is the algal biomass excluding carbohydrates and neutral lipids. The partitioning of the fixed carbon between the functional pool and the storage pool is regulated by the nitrogen cell quota $ Q_n $. We modeled the carbon fixation to the functional biomass ( $ R_1 $) in eq (1) based on the Droop model. $ ^{23} $ For simplicity, we modeled the degradation of functional biomass ( $ R_2 $) that contributes to respiration as a first-order relationship. The composition of functional biomass is assumed as $ CH_{1.8}O_{0.5}N_{0.2} $.

Symbols:
  A: Light absorbance per unit length [m^-1] (computed)
  a: Optical cross section of Chl-a [m^2 mol^-1 X_{chl}-C] (parameter)
  X_{chl}: Concentration of Chl-a as C [mol X_{chl}-C m^{-3}] (computed)
  b: Optical cross section of biomass except Chl-a content [m^2 mol^-1 C] (parameter)
  X_{C}: Total carbon concentration of the biomass [mol C m^{-3}] (variable)
  I_{avg}: Average light intensity inside the reactor [mol photons m^{-2} d^{-1}] (computed)
  z_{t}: Thickness of the photobioreactor along the optical path [m] (parameter)
  d: Distance from the light source to the front of the reactor [m] (parameter)
  I_{avg_R}: Reference average light intensity calculated without the absorbance term [mol photons m^{-2} d^{-1}] (computed)
  P: Photosynthesis rate normalized to functional biomass [mol C (mol X_{cd}-C)^{-1} d^{-1}] (computed)
  X_{cd}: Concentration of functional biomass (algal biomass excluding carbohydrates and neutral lipids) as C [mol X_{cd}-C m^{-3}] (computed)
  P_{m}: Maximum carbon fixation rate in the photosynthesis relation. [time^-1] (parameter)
  I_{sat}: Light saturation intensity used in the photosynthesis light-response relation. (computed)
  Y_{E}^{c}: Effective carbon yield on light energy after irradiance-dependent adjustment. [mol C (mol photons)^{-1}] (computed)
  Y_{E}: Carbon yield on light energy [mol C (mol photons)^{-1}] (parameter)
  k_{ye}: Coefficient controlling the irradiance-dependent exponential adjustment to carbon yield. (parameter)
  q_{nl}: Rate portion of carbon redirection from carbohydrate to lipid accumulation [unitless] (computed)
  \phi: Coefficient setting the amplitude of nitrate-dependent carbon redirection to neutral lipids. [-] (parameter)
  k_{N}: Coefficient controlling the nitrate-dependent error-function response. [m^3 (mol N)^{-1}] (parameter)
  S_{NO3}: Concentration of nitrate as N in the reactor [mol N m^{-3}] (computed)
  m_{chl}: Chl-a degradation rate (computed)
  m: Functional biomass degradation-rate constant (parameter)
  k_{I}: Light-dependent coefficient in the Chl-a degradation-rate expression (parameter)

Model-wide assumptions (already recorded, do not repeat):
  - Optical cross‑section parameters a and b are taken as constant regardless of cultivation conditions.
  - The composition of functional biomass is fixed to CH1.8O0.5N0.2.
  - Nitrate uptake is assumed to equal the nitrate removed from the medium.

laws.description: Light absorbance per unit length is computed from chlorophyll carbon and the remaining biomass carbon using their optical cross sections.
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies how biomass composition determines the optical absorbance used by the model.

laws.description: The reactor-average instantaneous light intensity is obtained by spatially averaging the attenuated light profile along the optical path.
laws.quote: is calculated by averaging the local light intensities
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies the light profile and attenuation used to calculate reactor-average irradiance.

laws.description: The reference average light intensity is calculated by averaging the unattenuated source-light profile along the optical path.
laws.quote: In addition, the average background light intensity
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies the source-light profile used to calculate the reference irradiance.

laws.description: Photosynthesis per unit functional biomass follows a Steele-type light response with light limitation and inhibition, scaled by the ratio of total to functional biomass.
laws.quote: which expresses the typical relationship between photosynthesis rate and light intensity (i.e., P-I relationship) during the stages of light limitation, saturation, and inhibition.
laws.law_type_reason: It gives the model's light-response kinetic expression for photosynthesis.

laws.description: The light saturation intensity is set by maximum fixation capacity relative to chlorophyll-associated conversion of light energy into fixed carbon.
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies a model relationship that sets the saturation intensity from photosynthetic and pigment quantities.

laws.description: The effective carbon yield on light energy decreases exponentially with reference average irradiance.
laws.law_type_reason: It gives an irradiance-dependent adjustment to the carbon yield.

laws.description: The fraction of carbon redirected from carbohydrate toward neutral-lipid accumulation is highest at low nitrate and decreases as nitrate increases.
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies a nitrate-dependent response for carbon redirection to neutral lipids.

laws.description: The Chl-a degradation rate increases with reference light intensity and nitrogen starvation through error-function responses.
laws.quote: to model the degradation of Chl-a under stress conditions because our experiments showed that the Chl-a concentration decreased under nitrogen starvation and high-light conditions
laws.law_type_reason: It specifies the stress-dependent kinetic expression for Chl-a degradation.
laws.issue: The term m is defined as the functional biomass degradation-rate constant, but eq 16 uses it to scale the Chl-a degradation rate.
